title: "About"
description: "Healthcare data science leader: background, how I work, and what I do outside the job."
---

I lead a data science team at Providence, helping leaders across a 50+ hospital system answer three questions: what's driving our outcomes, what's likely to happen next, and what should we do about it?

I started in healthcare strategy before moving into data science, so I start with the decision, not the model. Most of my work is causal inference, forecasting and risk prediction, along with the less glamorous part that comes after launch: keeping models useful, and retiring them when they no longer fit.

Some of my best ideas come from outside healthcare. Retail gravity models for how far patients will travel. Marketing attribution for care journeys. Queueing theory for capacity.

## How I work

- **Start with the decision.** Leaders should know what an analysis will change before it begins.
- **Pick the simplest method that answers the question.** Complexity has to earn its place.
- **Teach as I go.** I mentor data scientists at work and have taught statistics and data mining at BYU and the University of Utah.

## Beyond work

I served a two-year mission in coastal Ecuador, leading teams of volunteers and working entirely in Spanish, then taught Spanish for a year after I came home. These days my curiosity goes to sports (March Madness brackets, in-game decisions), trivia (I'm building a study system for a Jeopardy! audition), and a weekly underrated data visualization on [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/kayden-maughan/).
